clue.text: Study is the making of a fellow

parts.note: a den is a private study or snug room for working in

explanation.surface: Time spent studying is what makes a person into a proper fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Study' looks like a verb, but it is a noun here, a room. DENIS is a man's name, so it counts as 'a fellow' in crossword terms.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's first name stands for any male person, a chap, in crossword convention.

clue.text: The ambassador getting support at one point

parts.note: a leg is a support, as on a table or chair
E, for east, is one of the compass points

explanation.surface: A diplomat is being propped up at some stage of the proceedings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One point' looks like a moment in time; it is a point of the compass, E for east.
explanation.definitionFit: A legate is a papal envoy, a diplomat sent on a mission for the Pope.

clue.text: Looking about right, so taking the lead

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: staring is looking hard and fixedly

explanation.surface: Someone glancing round to the right as they move to the front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts R inside STARING.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor starring in a film plays its main role, the leading part.

clue.text: Odd name for the guy in charge!

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: odd means strange or irregular, so these letters are put into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A peculiar title to give to the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd' shuffles the letters of FOR and NAME.
explanation.definitionFit: A foreman supervises a team of workers, so he is the boss on site.

clue.text: He keeps on saying a salesman should go along with the consumer

parts.note: a rep, short for representative, is a travelling salesman
an eater is someone who consumes food

explanation.surface: Advice that a sales representative ought to accompany a customer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consumer' looks like a shopper, but here it means someone who eats.
explanation.definitionFit: A repeater is someone or something that says the same thing over and over.

clue.text: Incensed by transfer?

parts.note: cross means angry, incensed
by can mean over or past, as in 'the danger is by' meaning it is over

explanation.surface: Someone made furious by being moved to another post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Incensed' could suggest burning incense; it means angry. The question mark admits the loose sense of 'by' as OVER.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossover is a move or switch from one place, style or side to another.

clue.text: Admission price-note change is needed

indicators.note: change says these letters are altered into a different arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A notice saying the cost of entry has to be revised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' shuffles the letters of PRICE and NOTE together.
explanation.definitionFit: Reception is the act of receiving someone, letting them in, so it is entry or welcome.

clue.text: The natural growth of a summer's end in the garden plot

indicators.note: in places the small pieces inside the plot of ground

parts.note: a bed is a plot of ground in a garden for growing plants

indicators.note: end picks the final letter of the word summer's

explanation.surface: What a vegetable patch produces naturally once summer is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts A and R (the final letter of 'summer's') inside BED. 'Natural growth' suggests plants; it means hair on the chin.
explanation.definitionFit: Facial hair grows by itself on a man's chin unless shaved off.

clue.text: Many a doctor has a woolly coat

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty, a large number
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: Lots of physicians wear a fleecy overcoat.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description: the young sheep is the creature that has a woolly coat.
explanation.definitionFit: A young sheep is covered in fleece.

clue.text: Contend one's a king in the river

indicators.note: in places the pieces inside the river's name

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland, and another on the English-Welsh border
one is I, and 's adds S
GR, Georgius Rex, is the abbreviation for King George

explanation.surface: Claims that a monarch is standing in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contend' looks like fighting; here it means arguing. 'one's' supplies I plus the S of the possessive, and 'in' places them, with A and the king, inside the river.
explanation.definitionFit: To contend can mean to argue or dispute a point, to differ in opinion.

clue.text: Unwilling to read poetry

annotationWithheld.why: 'Unwilling to read poetry' (6): AVERSE looks like A VERSE, but no clue word gives the A and no indicator signals a sound-alike, so no fair parse.

clue.text: Some strikers like picketing in military gear

indicators.note: some says only part of the words is taken, letters running across them

explanation.surface: Several workers on strike enjoy standing on the picket line in army kit.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'liKE PIcketing'; 'strikers' is surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: A kepi is a French army cap with a flat round top and a peak.

clue.text: ____, the soldier's virtue." Shakespeare (Antony and Cleopatra)

definitions.text: ____, the soldier's virtue." Shakespeare (Antony and Cleopatra)

parts.words: ____, the soldier's virtue." Shakespeare (Antony and Cleopatra)
parts.note: a fill-in quotation: Ventidius in Antony and Cleopatra names the drive to rise as what a soldier prizes

explanation.definitionFit: The quotation names the desire for advancement and glory as the quality a soldier values.

clue.text: Yet Romans maybe found men in retreat here

indicators.note: maybe says the letters are one possible arrangement among others

explanation.surface: Roman soldiers might have found troops falling back at this spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' shuffles YET ROMANS. 'Retreat' suggests armies withdrawing; it means a place of religious seclusion.
explanation.definitionFit: A monastery is a secluded house where monks live apart from the world.

clue.text: A charge will be made after a certain time

parts.note: post is Latin for after, as in postwar
an age is a particular period of time

explanation.surface: A fee will be applied once some deadline has passed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charge' sounds like an accusation; it means a fee.
explanation.definitionFit: Postage is the fee paid for sending a letter or parcel.

clue.text: Concede to the French count

parts.note: le is French for the
to rate is to count or reckon, as in 'I rate him highly'

explanation.surface: Admitting something to a French nobleman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'count' suggests a French nobleman; it is a verb, to rate.
explanation.definitionFit: To tolerate is to allow or put up with something, giving way on it.

clue.text: The way to encompass exceptionally clear colour

indicators.note: to encompass means to surround, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: ST, street, is the abbreviation for a road or way

indicators.note: exceptionally hints the word is put into an unusual order

explanation.surface: A road surrounding a remarkably bright shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exceptionally' rearranges the letters of 'clear', and 'to encompass' wraps the street abbreviation round them. 'The way' is a street, not a method.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarlet is a brilliant red.

clue.text: Only after money-that's material

indicators.note: after puts the word for only behind the word for money

parts.note: cash is money
mere means only, nothing more than

explanation.surface: Someone saying all they want is cash, and that's what matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'material' looks like the adjective meaning important; it is fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Cashmere is a fine soft wool fabric from Kashmir goats.

clue.text: Threats can seem ridiculous

indicators.note: ridiculous says the letters are put into an absurd new order

explanation.surface: Threatening behaviour can look absurd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ridiculous' shuffles CAN SEEM.
explanation.definitionFit: Menaces are threats of harm, as in 'demanding money with menaces'.

clue.text: Talk of the standard cut

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level, as in golf
to lance is to cut open with a blade

explanation.surface: Discussion about the usual reduction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' looks like a noun; it is a verb, to lance.
explanation.definitionFit: Parlance is a way of speaking, particular jargon or idiom.

clue.text: In one's true home

indicators.note: in says the letters are found inside the following words

explanation.surface: In your own genuine house.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'oNE'S True'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird's nest is its home; the word also means a cosy dwelling.

clue.text: He's taking legal proceedings about American backing

indicators.note: backing means the pieces run in the opposite direction

parts.note: re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A litigant who is supporting an American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' looks like support for an American, but it turns the two pieces round together. The definition 'He's taking legal proceedings' is a whole phrase for one who sues.
explanation.definitionFit: One who brings a lawsuit against another is a plaintiff or litigant.

clue.text: Expire, though previously fit as a fiddle

parts.note: ex means former, previously
hale means in robust good health

explanation.surface: Someone dying though they used to be in perfect health.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Expire' suggests dying; here it means breathing out.
explanation.definitionFit: To expire literally means to breathe out.

clue.text: Premier taking rebel leader in hand

indicators.note: in puts the initial inside the word for hand

parts.note: a fist is a clenched hand

indicators.note: leader picks the opening letter of the word rebel, the one at its head

parts.note: the word from which the opening letter is taken

explanation.surface: A prime minister seizing the chief insurgent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Premier' looks like a prime minister but is the adjective meaning foremost.
explanation.definitionFit: Premier as an adjective means leading or foremost, top of the list.

clue.text: Supplies rushed into a sea-going vessel

indicators.note: into places the word for rushed inside the ship

parts.note: SS, steamship, prefixes ships' names
tore means ran fast, rushed

explanation.surface: Provisions were hurried aboard a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Stores are stocks of provisions kept for use.

clue.text: March in good order to music-find comfort in it

indicators.note: in good order says the letters are arranged afresh

parts.note: an air is a tune, a piece of music

explanation.surface: Soldiers parade smartly to a band and then relax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in good order' shuffles MARCH into ARMCH.
explanation.definitionFit: An easy chair with arm rests is a comfortable seat.

clue.text: Bars that cause some irritation?

definitions.meaning: a frame of metal bars holding a fire
to rasp or annoy, getting on someone's nerves

explanation.definitionFit: A fireplace grid is a set of bars; to irk or annoy someone is the second sense.

clue.text: Not feeling a shelter's called for

indicators.note: called for here suggests the letters are summoned into a new order

parts.note: the word with its S counted as a letter

explanation.surface: Lack of compassion means a refuge is needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'called for' shuffles the nine letters of A SHELTER'S, the S of the possessive counting.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone without pity or compassion is cold and cruel.
